key_findings: **FUN_0076A3F0 is a SHARED Receiver state-cache lazy-init helper used by 18 different factories.** Not VehicleGrade-specific. The 0xCC=204-byte cached object at container+0x48 holds inline state mirrors for ~18 Receiver state fields (one per caller).

**The hybrid factory pattern generalizes from VehicleGrade to a broader Receiver factory layer.** VehicleGradeReceiver::HybridFactory (BCS-Y-1145) has a fast-path/slow-path branch on container[+0x50] flag. With 18 callers of FUN_0076A3F0, the same fast-path/slow-path optimization likely applies to all 18 Receiver types - meaning ~17 more Receiver classes have hybrid factories with the same shape.

**Architectural implication**: the Receiver instantiation surface has TWO layers - (a) the slow-path simple factories that allocate a Receiver instance, and (b) the fast-path direct-write to a cached state mirror. The choice between them is gated by a container flag, likely set based on whether the receiver is needed for queued processing (e.g. command-stream playback) vs immediate apply (e.g. state-changed broadcast).

**The 0xCC-byte cache layout** holds inline byte/dword fields for the 18 caller Receivers' state. VehicleGrade has its inline byte at cache+0xB8. The other 17 fields would map to different cache offsets per caller. Later work could decomp FUN_00767730 (the cache init function) and the 18 callers to produce a full cache field-layout map.

**Builds on client-architecture 'Real implementations with no static caller are structurally legitimate'** (real-impl-no-caller pattern). The hybrid factories (BCS-Y-1145 and similar) ARE the canonical real-impl-no-caller shape - zero direct instruction-level callers, reached via function-pointer table dispatch. The state-cache layer underneath is the IMPLEMENTATION side that explains how factories can be 'dead' from a static-caller perspective yet load-bearing at runtime: the cached state mirror is read via different code paths (e.g. Lua getters, UI render loops) that don't statically reference the factories.

**Builds on client-architecture 'Sqwt UI elements follow a uniform heap-factory'** (Sqwt UI subscription pattern). The Receiver factory layer's cache mirror pattern is a Receiver-side analog of the Element-side subscription pattern: both are mechanisms by which the C++ runtime maintains state-and-callback collections without each component needing to know the full picture of every other component.
